question: What is the primary role of pharmacotherapy in inherited degenerative diseases?

options.B: To modulate pathways, compensate for deficiencies, or manage symptoms
options.C: To cure the underlying cellular degeneration permanently
options.D: To accelerate the rate of tissue regeneration

explanation: Pharmacotherapy in these conditions rarely offers a cure; instead, it is designed to interact with altered biological pathways, compensate for deficiencies, or modulate imbalances. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h1)

question: Why is recognizing disease progression staging critical when starting drug therapy for degenerative conditions?

options.A: Medication efficacy often varies depending on how far cellular deterioration has advanced
options.B: Staging determines the exact financial cost of the drugs
options.C: Advanced stages mean medications are no longer administered by nurses
options.D: Staging replaces the need for baseline nursing assessments

explanation: The text notes that evaluating disease progression staging is vital because the efficacy of many degenerative disease medications varies depending on how far cellular deterioration has advanced. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h1)

question: What is the primary aim of disease-modifying therapies in inherited degenerative conditions?

options.A: To completely eradicate the genetic mutation
options.B: To slow underlying pathophysiological processes and prolong independence
options.C: To provide immediate, permanent relief from all physical pain
options.D: To replace the need for physical and occupational therapy

explanation: Disease-modifying therapies aim to slow the underlying pathophysiological processes, alter the natural history of the condition, and prolong independent functioning. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h2)

question: How can nurses objectively evaluate if a disease-modifying regimen is working over time?

options.A: By documenting functional baselines using validated rating scales
options.B: By asking the family how much money they have spent on drugs
options.C: By stopping the medication periodically to check for sudden cures
options.D: By relying solely on the patient's subjective feelings without records

explanation: Documenting functional baselines using validated rating scales enables the healthcare team to objectively evaluate whether a disease-modifying regimen is achieving its intended goals. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of symptomatic management medications in degenerative diseases?

options.A: To alter the underlying genetic mutation permanently
options.B: To reverse cellular deterioration in organ systems
options.C: To alleviate secondary burdens like pain and spasticity to improve quality of life
options.D: To shorten the duration of the disease process

explanation: Symptomatic medications do not alter underlying progression, but they alleviate secondary burdens such as spasticity, pain, and depression to improve daily comfort and quality of life. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h3)

question: How can effective symptomatic control impact family caregivers in resource-constrained settings?

options.A: It can significantly reduce caregiver burnout by easing daily care demands
options.B: It eliminates the need for any further nursing involvement
options.C: It forces caregivers to take over physician prescribing duties
options.D: It increases the physical burden of turning and feeding patients

explanation: Effective symptomatic control can significantly reduce caregiver burnout by easing the physical and emotional demands of daily nursing care tasks like turning, feeding, and mobility support. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h3)

question: What does pharmacokinetics specifically study regarding drug therapy?

options.A: The biochemical mechanisms and receptor sensitivity of drugs
options.B: The absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of drugs
options.C: The genetic mutations that cause degenerative diseases
options.D: The psychological impact of chronic illness on family members

explanation: Pharmacokinetics involves the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) of drugs within the body. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h4)

question: Why must nurses be especially vigilant about pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic changes in patients with degenerative conditions?

options.A: Because target receptor sensitivity and organ clearance can be altered, risking toxicity
options.B: Because PK and PD principles only apply to pediatric patients in Nigeria
options.C: Because laboratory serum drug levels are always immediately available
options.D: Because body composition never changes in chronic degenerative illnesses

explanation: Altered organ function affects ADME, and ongoing cellular loss can make receptors hypersensitive or desensitized, requiring clinical vigilance to prevent toxicity or therapeutic failure. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h4)

question: What is a major risk when patients with degenerative disorders take multiple prescriptions for various symptoms?

options.A: Polypharmacy and increased potential for adverse drug interactions
options.B: Immediate and complete genetic cure of the disease
options.C: Elimination of the need for baseline nursing assessments

explanation: Patients with degenerative disorders frequently take multiple prescriptions, which increases the risk of polypharmacy and adverse interactions. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h5)

question: What specific safety precaution must a nurse take for a patient with dysphagia taking oral medications?

options.A: Force the patient to swallow large capsules dry without water
options.B: Assess swallowing ability and consult on safe route modifications like liquid formulations
options.C: Stop all medications permanently without notifying the physician
options.D: Delegate administration entirely to untrained visitors

explanation: Patients with swallowing disorders are at risk for aspiration, requiring nurses to assess swallowing and consult on safe modifications like crushing or liquids after pharmacist verification. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h5)

question: Why are patients with degenerative diseases particularly susceptible to drug toxicity?

options.A: Because many of their medications have narrow therapeutic indices and potential organ impairment
options.B: Because they eliminate drugs faster than healthy individuals
options.C: Because they never experience changes in liver or kidney function
options.D: Because they only take herbal supplements instead of pharmaceuticals

explanation: Many disease-modifying and symptomatic medications have narrow therapeutic indices, making patients susceptible to toxicity especially with subclinical organ impairment. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h6)

question: What is the appropriate immediate nursing action when an adverse drug reaction is suspected?

options.A: Double the next dose to build up patient tolerance
options.B: Withhold the offending medication and notify the attending physician
options.C: Wait until the next scheduled clinic appointment to mention it
options.D: Instruct the family to stop all monitoring permanently

explanation: When an ADR is suspected, the nurse must act promptly by withholding the offending medication, notifying the physician, and documenting the event. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h6)

question: What is a primary driver of medication non-adherence in many Nigerian households dealing with chronic illnesses?

options.A: Economic constraints and out-of-pocket health expenditures
options.B: An excess of free financial resources provided by hospitals
options.C: The complete absence of any side effects from drugs
options.D: Rapid, miraculous cures that make ongoing pills unnecessary

explanation: Economic constraints and out-of-pocket health expenditures mean that medication cost is a primary driver of non-adherence in many households. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h7)

question: Why is it critical to educate patients and families against abruptly discontinuing their degenerative disease medications?

options.A: Sudden cessation can trigger severe withdrawal syndromes or acute disease exacerbations
options.B: Abrupt stopping immediately cures the underlying genetic mutation
options.C: It prevents nurses from having to document medication administration
options.D: It guarantees that the cost of medications will decrease

explanation: Families must be warned against abruptly stopping medications because sudden cessation can trigger severe withdrawal syndromes or acute disease exacerbations. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h7)
